note: Set A and Set B contain exactly the same 25 claims with identical values, conditions and quotes; the only difference is the ordering of the HSS4X6X1/4 and 9'-0" entries. Both correctly capture the member sections, the two drawing scales with their elevation titles, the solar envelope and T.O. STEEL elevations, and the plate size. Both also share the same weaknesses: repeated dimension claims (9'-0" and 2'-4" each appear twice) and a plate claim that restates the PL3"X1/4" section claim, plus many bare dimension values with no component or property binding. Because the content is identical, neither set is better.
remarks: Both sets are content-identical (only claim order differs). Shared issues: dimension claims such as 'dimension | value | 8"' or 'dimension | length | 9'-0"' carry no component or what-is-measured binding, so they are vague and not verifiable against a specific detail; 'plate | size | 3"X1/4"' duplicates the PL3"X1/4" section claim; 9'-0" and 2'-4" are each claimed twice. Both also omit notable dimensions on the page (e.g. 32'-0", 27'-8", 7'-6", 5'-6", 3'-1", 10'-0", 7 7/8", 3") and the FIRST FLR 2'-4" / GRADE LEVEL 0" datums. Entity naming is inconsistent ('member' vs 'structural member' vs 'plate' vs 'steel'), and the text layer loses the spatial association between dimensions and the members they size, which is likely why the extractors left dimensions unbound.
